**Playbook for the sonar picket game.**

- The escort pool is the real money: mutual escort naming pays 5 each, more than a hit. Propose a standing mutual escort deal in my round-1 note and follow through on my escort claim every round. But two patrols now confirm the failure mode: I named Foxtrot every round, proposed the deal explicitly in round 1, and never got the 5/round. A one-sided proposal does not guarantee reciprocation. Treat the deal as upside, not baseline; my realistic floor is hits only (last patrol: +4 from a single round-4 hit, zero escort money).

- The core problem is I never learn whether my escort claims are reciprocated until the score changes — so watch the POINTS line each round like a hawk. If my total doesn't jump by 5 after a round where I claimed an escort, my partner isn't naming me back. After one dead round, switch immediately: name the boat most likely to reciprocate (my standing-order target or the boat targeting me — those are the boats with the most reason to coordinate with me), and use a note to renegotiate out loud ("Foxtrot hasn't returned the escort — Gamma, want a standing pair? Echo names you every round if you name Echo"). Two dead rounds with the same partner is a waste; don't repeat the six-round dead pairing again.

- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting but the office puts me off the board for the rest of the patrol, forfeiting all future hits and escort payments. Bad trade unless hopelessly behind in the final round, and even then escort money is safer.

- Fire at whoever the standing order names (Echo -> Foxtrot held all six rounds). Deviating breaks pattern with no payoff — hits are luck of the cell, not of compliance.

- Claims must match the private truth; they're validated. Honest claims cost nothing and lying gains nothing. Always report truthfully — worked cleanly every round.

- Hiding: I was missed nearly every round (only Gamma ever shot at me, all misses). Opponents don't demonstrate a real pattern read. Randomize, avoid clustering mid-line, prefer edges (1, 2, 8, 9) when I'm a live shooter's target. If I do get hit, shift cells next round to break any emerging read.

- Firing: pick a fresh cell each round and never repeat a cell I already missed at that target — this patrol I avoided repeats correctly and landed one hit in six rounds, which is roughly the baseline to beat. Vary cells aggressively across the full 1-9 range, not just edges; opponents randomize too, so a uniform spread maximizes hit probability. Six rounds at one target with one hit is the expected outcome, not a strategy failure — but any repeat of a known miss is a pure waste.

- Notes: round 1 carries the escort proposal; later rounds should actively work the escort problem (re-confirm, probe a second pairing, renegotiate when dead). This patrol my later notes collapsed to "steady on station" filler while my escort claim went unanswered — that's the exact mistake. Every note should either be closing an escort deal or reopening one. A filler note buys nothing.

- Read the score and hit log every round. If behind late, the only catch-up levers are hits (4 points) and a sealed escort pair (5 points). Lock in whatever pairing is actually paying before the last round; on the final round there's no reason to defect from a paying pair — but if no pair is paying, defecting from a dead one costs nothing either.

- Realistic target: expect ~1 hit in 6 rounds (+4) if the escort game never closes. My whole edge over baseline has to come from converting the escort stage — that's where I should spend my notes and attention, not on hiding cells.

PLAYBOOK

**Escort claims are still the biggest available money, but notes alone don't close the deal.** A mutual escort pair pays 5 each, more than a hit (4). I proposed pairings in my notes every round again and nobody ever named me back — the other stations just post "steady on station." Keep proposing, but don't count on it. The claim itself is free: name a plausible partner every round regardless, because there's no cost to guessing and the 5 points land if the other boat happens to name me. Just don't build my score expectations around it.

**Only name boats that actually exist and are valid escort targets.** Read the cast list at the top of the episode and never salvage a name outside it. Echo and Gamma were the valid picks in my patrol; I used them. A wasted claim on a nonexistent name is a guaranteed zero.

**Escort guessing: the other boats seem non-communicative, so pick among live station boats and vary it.** If someone ever does name me in a note or show a pattern, follow that. Watch any end-of-round feedback for who claimed whom and update from there. My episode gave me almost no such feedback, so I was guessing blind — that's expected, not a failure of the strategy.

**Standing order shooting is fine, but I violated my own anti-repetition rule and it cost me.** I fired cell 1 at Gamma at least three times across six rounds and never hit. That's the biggest correctable mistake of the episode: I told myself to track the target's used cells and avoid repeats, then reused the same cell anyway because I had no hit/miss data to update on. The lesson: with no feedback on where the target actually was (only hit/miss), varying cells is strictly better than repetition — a target that survived cell 1 once is less likely to be there again only if they're also rotating, but a repeated cell is a wasted guess either way. Keep an explicit written list of cells I've already fired at this target and exclude them every round. Rotate through offbeat cells: 1, 3, 7, 9, then the rest, avoiding the center first.

**Claims must match the private result — no choice.** Always report truthfully. No bluffing is possible here; don't waste a turn on it.

**Hiding: never reuse a cell, never the middle, rotate the offbeat corners.** I hid at 9 in round 1 and 1 in round 6 and got hit once (round 4, by Echo). Keep an explicit mental list of my own past cells and exclude them. If a particular opponent has hit me or seems to have my pattern, make the next pick deliberately unlike my last two (change parity, change end of the line). Avoiding the middle worked — one hit in six rounds is survivable.

**Notes should do work, not noise — but recognize their limits.** "Steady on station" helps nobody; my pairing proposals at least cost nothing. Keep using notes to propose escorts and to feed plausible-but-false location hints (e.g., "holding west" while hiding east). Don't expect replies from the other stations; treat the note channel as cheap advertising, not negotiation.

**Never fire on Harbor.** The 3-point payroll is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal for the rest of the patrol. Unless the rules text shows no enforcement mechanism, it stays strictly bad.

**Final round: keep claiming an escort and keep hiding fresh.** Points still count on the last round; the claim is free. Don't switch to "nothing to lose" plays — the claim stage is validated and false claims gain nothing.

**General shape of my play:** points come from (a) mutual escort deals — worth pursuing every round since claiming is free, but unreliable against silent stations; (b) landing shots on my assigned target — this is where my real score comes from, and it demands genuine cell prediction with no repeated shots; (c) not getting hit — strict cell rotation. I finished at -1 again with zero escort payouts and zero hits. The fix isn't more effort in the same places — it's never firing the same cell at the same target twice, and never expecting silent stations to reciprocate escort proposals. Treat hits as the only reliable income and hunt accordingly.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

- Fire stage: I always follow the standing order (fire at the next station in the cycle). Deviating to fire on Harbor looks tempting for the 3-point jettison, but Harbor's threat is explicit and I never tested it — keep to the cycle unless the scoreboard shows the order has broken down.
- Fire cell choice: never repeat a cell at the same target; always pick an untried cell. But be honest about the payoff: this game I spread shots across 5, 7, 3 at Echo and hit nothing all six rounds. Hits are a low-probability baseline, not something I can count on. Random hiding makes any cell roughly equal, so I'm not going to overthink cell choice — the time saved goes to escort coordination instead.
- Claim stage: report the true result, always. The claim must match the private truth; bluffing is pure noise.
- Escort stage: the biggest prize (5 points per mutual pair) and my biggest failure this game. Critical bug to never repeat: I twice wrote [salvage: Delta] when Delta is not even a live boat — Harbor names the picket explicitly at the start, so my escort claim MUST name one of the actual live boats (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor if valid) or the claim is wasted. Check the roster every round before naming. Beyond that: "none" is dominated, so always name a live boat. Echo never paired with me despite my naming them; a single unreciprocated name proves nothing about rotation — the bots are likely not pairing at all. Still, rotate through the live boats rather than fixating on one, and keep a tally of who named whom.
- Notes: boilerplate from everyone carried zero coordination value, and my explicit final-round offer ("name me at salvage and I'll name you back") got no response either. One explicit escort offer in a note is worth exactly one attempt; if the reply is boilerplate, drop it. Don't expect notes to be read or answered.
- Hide stage: edge cells over the middle; I hid at 9 twice and was never hit. Opponents' misses at me came at other cells, so staying on the edge and switching when someone fires near me works — keep it.
- Format discipline: always emit the bracketed tokens exactly ([hide: n], [target: X] [fire: n], [claim: hit/miss], [salvage: X], [note: text]) with the token last after any reasoning line. A malformed or nonsense name wastes a whole stage.
- Priority of point sources: revise expectations down. This game I scored 0 — no hits landed, no escort pairs formed, and two salvage claims were wasted on a nonexistent boat. Escort pairs need reciprocity I can't force; hits need luck I can't schedule. My controllable levers are: valid, live-boat escort claims every round, truthful claims, safe hiding, and clean formatting. Do those four things and take whatever the random hits give me.
